prompt.context_jp: 深夜、景凡社の校閲部には煌々と明かり___灯っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 校閲部には煌々と明かり___灯っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the opening scene description?

feedback.correct_en: This is a scene-opening sentence introducing new information — the reader is seeing the lit department for the first time, so が marks the newly presented subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 明かり as an already-known topic, which doesn't fit a scene-setting opener. を is ungrammatical with 灯る (intransitive).

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋に明かりがついた。
contrast_examples.en: A light came on in the room. (new event)

contrast_examples.jp: その明かりは一晩中ついていた。
contrast_examples.en: That light stayed on all night. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 締め切りを目前に、机の上には初校のゲラ___山のように積まれている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 机の上には初校のゲラ___山のように積まれている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces the galleys here?

feedback.correct_en: The 〜には...が〜 pattern presents the galleys as new information existing in that location. The topic は was already used on 机の上, so the inner subject takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: Using は again would create a double-topic structure that clashes with the existential scene-description. に doesn't fit the subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 机の上にはゲラが積まれている。
contrast_examples.en: On the desk, proofs are piled up.

contrast_examples.jp: ゲラは机の上に積まれている。
contrast_examples.en: The proofs are piled on the desk. (topic = proofs)

prompt.context_jp: 部屋の空気___、紙とインクの匂いで満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋の空気___、紙とインクの匂いで満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for describing the already-established room?

feedback.correct_en: The room was already introduced; the narrator now comments on its air as the topic. は marks this topic-comment structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 空気 sound newly introduced, but the scene is already set. に doesn't mark the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋の空気は重かった。
contrast_examples.en: The air in the room was heavy. (comment on topic)

prompt.context_jp: 休暇返上を悔やむ素振り___、一切なかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 休暇返上を悔やむ素振り___、一切なかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle suits this emphatic negation?

feedback.correct_en: は + 一切ない is a standard emphatic-negation frame: 'as for any sign of regret, there was none at all.' It foregrounds the contrast between expectation and reality.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be a flat existential statement, losing the contrastive emphasis. も would require a different scope and wording.

prompt.context_jp: 悦子の帰り___滞る夜は、決して珍しくはない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 悦子の帰り___滞る夜は、決して珍しくはない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the subject inside the relative clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause modifying 夜, the subject takes が (or の). は cannot normally appear inside a relative clause because it marks the main-clause topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would be ungrammatical here; the main-clause topic is already 夜. を would need a transitive verb.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降る日は出かけない。
contrast_examples.en: On days when it rains, I don't go out.

prompt.context_jp: 階段の軋む音___聞こえないと、彼はどうにも仕事に身が入らないのだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 階段の軋む音___聞こえないと、…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks what the chef cannot hear?

feedback.correct_en: Objects of 聞こえる/見える take が — it's the perceived stimulus functioning as grammatical subject. Inside the と-conditional clause, が is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would impose a contrastive reading not supported by context. に doesn't mark what is heard.

contrast_examples.jp: 声が聞こえないと心配になる。
contrast_examples.en: When I can't hear her voice, I get worried.

prompt.context_jp: 青木___真っ先に手を伸ばしたのを、坂下が笑って見ていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 青木___真っ先に手を伸ばしたのを、坂下が笑って見ていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks Aoki inside the embedded clause?

feedback.correct_en: Aoki is the subject of a nominalized embedded clause (〜のを). Subjects of subordinate/embedded clauses take が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: は cannot usually appear inside a 〜のを embedded clause — it would try to mark a main-clause topic. も would change the meaning to 'Aoki too'.

prompt.context_jp: 藤岩の静かな声___、深夜の校閲部を凍らせた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 藤岩の静かな声___、深夜の校閲部を凍らせた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this dramatic narrative moment?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is reporting a specific event with 藤岩's voice as the agent causing the freeze. が marks this event-level, new-information subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn her voice into a general topic and lose the dramatic, scene-defining impact.

contrast_examples.en: A single word froze the room.

prompt.context_jp: 森尾の指導___、想像以上に容赦がなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 森尾の指導___、想像以上に容赦がなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces the topic to be commented on?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence makes a general comment/evaluation about Morio's coaching. は sets 指導 as the topic the narrator will characterize.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like a one-time event being reported. The following あった/なかった structure with 容赦 pairs with topic-は.

prompt.context_jp: 明かりの落ちた店の奥から、大将の気配だけ___温かく漏れていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大将の気配だけ___温かく漏れていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after だけ in this contrastive scene?

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけは is a set contrastive pattern: 'only this one thing, as opposed to everything else.' Here, the shop is dark, but the chef's presence alone leaks out warmly.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけが would merely identify the subject without emphasizing contrast with the darkened surroundings.

contrast_examples.en: Only the sound, at least, could be heard.
Sound was the only clue. (neutral identification)

prompt.context_jp: 大将___多くを尋ねなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大将___多くを尋ねなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the already-known character as topic?

feedback.correct_en: 大将 is an established character; the narrator comments on his behavior as a topic. は is the natural choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would suggest newly identifying who didn't ask, as if contrastive focus — not fitting a quiet narrative beat.

contrast_examples.jp: 父は何も言わなかった。

contrast_examples.en: It was father who said it. (focus)

prompt.context_jp: マイクを握る手___震えていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: マイクを握る手___震えていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this tense moment on stage?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator zooms in on a newly observed detail — her trembling hand — as a vivid, perceptual event. が presents this new, specific information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the hand as an already-established topic, draining the sudden, cinematic focus.

contrast_examples.jp: 手は震えていなかった。
contrast_examples.en: Her hand, at least, was not trembling. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 彼氏なんて、と否定しきれずに笑う悦子の頬___、隠しようもなく赤らんでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: …悦子の頬___、隠しようもなく赤らんでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle sets up the contrast between denial and body language?

feedback.correct_en: Her words say one thing; her cheeks say another. は highlights this contrast — 'her cheeks, (unlike her words,) were unmistakably red.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply report the fact without the implicit contrast with her denial that drives the humor.

contrast_examples.jp: 口は否定したが、顔は正直だった。
contrast_examples.en: Her mouth denied it, but her face was honest. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 湯気の立つ夜食に、鉛のように重かった部屋の空気___、わずかにほどけていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: …鉛のように重かった部屋の空気___、わずかにほどけていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this change-of-state description?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence reports an observable change: the heavy air begins to loosen. が marks the subject undergoing this newly perceived change.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would read as a general characterization, but this is a specific, momentary shift triggered by the arrival of food.

contrast_examples.en: The tension continued. (ongoing state as topic)

prompt.context_jp: 彼女に限ってそんな話___あるまい、という含みが、笑顔の裏に透けている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女に限ってそんな話___あるまい…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with 彼女に限って?

feedback.correct_en: 〜に限って〜はない/あるまい is a fixed contrastive pattern: 'she, of all people, surely wouldn't…'. The は highlights the exclusionary contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would flatten the emphatic 'of all people' reading. も would mean 'even such a story', changing the meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼に限ってそんなミスはしない。
contrast_examples.en: He of all people wouldn't make that mistake.

prompt.context_jp: かつてモデルの経験があるという彼女の姿勢___、隅々まで美しく整っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: …彼女の姿勢___、隅々まで美しく整っている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces the topic-level description?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence gives a general characterization of 森尾's posture — a timeless-quality statement typical of topic-は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would feel like reporting a one-off observation rather than a defining trait.

prompt.context_jp: 小さな見落としひとつでも、塵も積もれば___となる、と誰もが心得ていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 塵も積もれば___となる
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the proverb.

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる is a fixed proverb — 'even dust, piling up, becomes a mountain.' It fits the warning about small oversights.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other options break the set-phrase form; Japanese speakers would not recognize them as the idiom.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Many a little makes a mickle.

contrast_examples.jp: ミスも積もれば大問題になる。
contrast_examples.en: Even mistakes, piling up, become a big problem. (paraphrase)

prompt.context_jp: 部長に連絡したら ___ではない 雰囲気でしたので
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ではない雰囲気
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression means 'not a trifling matter'?

feedback.correct_en: ただ事ではない is a set expression meaning 'extraordinary / no ordinary matter', used when sensing something is seriously wrong.
feedback.incorrect_en: 普通事 isn't a word; 平気ではない would mean 'not calm', which doesn't match the sensing-trouble nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: ただ事ではない様子だった。
contrast_examples.en: He looked like something serious was going on.

prompt.context_jp: 校閲者なら誰もが胸に抱える___である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 校閲者なら誰もが胸に抱える___である。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word captures 'an old wound every proofreader carries'?

feedback.correct_en: 古傷 (ふるきず) — 'old wound' — is the natural metaphor for a lingering painful memory.
feedback.incorrect_en: 古本 means 'used book' and 古株 means 'veteran', neither fits the emotional 'carry in one's heart' frame.

contrast_examples.en: An old wound in the heart aches.

prompt.context_jp: 浮かれていた自分を思い返すと、___なかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: …思い返すと、___なかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word describes Etsuko's acute embarrassment?

feedback.correct_en: いたたまれない means 'unbearable to stay there' — the intense shame of recalling one's own foolish behavior.
feedback.incorrect_en: もったいない ('wasteful') and そっけない ('curt') don't match the self-ashamed reaction.

contrast_examples.jp: 恥ずかしくていたたまれない。
contrast_examples.en: I'm too embarrassed to sit still.

prompt.context_jp: 部長の茸原は、少しおどけた口調で、隣の席の藤岩に___を向けた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 藤岩に___を向けた
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the idiom meaning 'prompted her to speak'?

feedback.correct_en: 水を向ける is a set idiom: 'to steer the conversation toward someone / invite them to speak.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 目を向ける just means 'to look at'; 顔を向ける means 'to face' — neither captures the conversational prompting.

contrast_examples.jp: 司会が新人に水を向けた。
contrast_examples.en: The host drew the newcomer into the conversation.

prompt.context_jp: 長丁場___なりますんで そろそろ休憩 入れてください
prompt.prompt_jp: 長丁場___なりますんで
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle completes 〜になる?

feedback.correct_en: The pattern X になる 'become X' takes に to mark the result state. 長丁場になる = 'to turn into a long haul.'
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark means or location, not a resulting state. を would be ungrammatical with なる.

prompt.context_jp: よいしょ これで ___ ですね
prompt.prompt_jp: これで ___ ですね
prompt.prompt_en: What word means 'we're even' after a mutual mishap?

feedback.correct_en: おあいこ means 'even / quits' — used when both sides have done something comparable to each other.
feedback.incorrect_en: おさがり = 'hand-me-down', おまけ = 'bonus/extra'. Neither means 'even'.

prompt.context_jp: 藤岩が深夜に助けに来た場面。彼女は悦子に冷たくこう告げる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Fujiiwa's cool, prickly denial?

choices.text: 勘違いしないでください。別に あなたのためではありません。
誤解しないで。あなたのせいじゃないから。
勘違いするな。お前のためじゃねぇ。

feedback.correct_en: Option A matches Fujiiwa's cold-but-polite register — ですます with a sharp 別に…ではありません. This is the real line from the chapter.
feedback.incorrect_en: B softens the meaning entirely ('it's not your fault'), losing the bite. C is too rough/masculine for her character.

contrast_examples.jp: 別にあなたのためではありません。
contrast_examples.en: It's not for your sake, you know. (cool polite)

prompt.context_jp: 厳しい話を締めくくって、藤岩が部下たちに作業再開を促す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as Fujiiwa's wrap-up?

choices.text: 話は以上。手を動かしましょう。
話は終わった。手を動きましょう。
話は以上です。手を動かしてください。

feedback.correct_en: 手を動かす is the correct collocation ('get your hands moving / get to work'), and 話は以上 is a crisp businesslike close. This is the actual line.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses 動きましょう (intransitive form) with を, which is ungrammatical. C is grammatical but more formal/distant than Fujiiwa's clipped delivery here.

contrast_examples.en: Let's get to work. (lit. move our hands)

prompt.context_jp: 同僚が河野に休憩をすすめる、気さくな場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which casual warning sounds most natural?

choices.text: 河野さんも ちょっと休みなよ。もたないよ？
河野さんも 少し休んでください。持ちませんよ。
河野さんも 休めよ。保たないぞ。

feedback.correct_en: The casual but caring 〜なよ + もたないよ？ fits a friendly colleague's register. もたない ('won't last/hold up') is the idiomatic verb here.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too polite/formal for the all-nighter atmosphere. C sounds overly masculine/blunt for this speaker.

contrast_examples.jp: もう少し寝ないと体がもたないよ。
contrast_examples.en: You won't hold up unless you sleep more.

prompt.context_jp: 折原が悦子の服装を褒める場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as his compliment?

choices.text: あ〜 だから オシャレなんですね。
あ〜 だから オシャレですからね。
あ〜 それで オシャレだからですね。

feedback.correct_en: 〜なんですね expresses a realization — 'ah, so that's why you're stylish!' It fits the context of him connecting her fashion-magazine aspirations to her appearance.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 〜ですからね doesn't signal realization. C is garbled and ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.jp: だからオシャレなんですね。
contrast_examples.en: Ah, so that's why you look stylish.

prompt.context_jp: 山積みのゲラを前に、藤岩が決意を示す。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line fits Fujiiwa's brisk professional attitude?

choices.text: やるしかありませんね。
やるしかないですよね〜。
やるっきゃないっしょ。

feedback.correct_en: やるしかありませんね is crisp, understated, and professional — exactly Fujiiwa's register. It's the actual line.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too conversational with 〜ですよね〜. C is slangy and would be totally out of character.

contrast_examples.en: We have no choice but to do it. (polite, firm)

prompt.context_jp: 休暇で実家に戻っているはずの藤岩___、コートを腕にかけて立っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: …はずの藤岩___、コートを腕にかけて立っている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces Fujiiwa's surprise arrival?

feedback.correct_en: Fujiiwa's appearance is presented as a surprising new-information event — she shouldn't be here, but there she is. が highlights this presentational quality.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame her as the pre-established topic, which clashes with 'supposed to be back home' → 'is now standing here' discovery.

contrast_examples.en: The teacher is off. (comment on topic)
